lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Make the code link a complete, working URL that leads to relevant work.
items.because: The repositories or portfolio should be directly accessible and understandable.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are generally irrelevant to technical hiring and can create bias or privacy concerns.

items.says: Consider adding a specialization, thesis, or relevant coursework if it adds new information.
items.because: It could help when the degree is highly relevant to the target role.

items.says: Be ready to clarify how the degree program fits alongside the internship.
items.because: The overlapping dates may raise questions about whether the program is full-time, part-time, or structured around employment.

items.says: Standardize the location format used for the institutions.
items.because: “Metro City, USA” and “Metro City, Country” look inconsistent.

items.says: Consider adding honors, a strong GPA, or relevant coursework if competitive and space permits.
Define the accuracy metric and the comparison baseline for the 35% improvement.
items.because: “Accuracy” can mean many things, and the improvement is difficult to assess without a metric and baseline.

items.says: Clarify the size and nature of the evaluation data.
items.because: It would make the accuracy result easier to assess.

items.says: Give the business or model outcome more emphasis than the training details.
items.because: “Validated tool-use trajectories” and “assistant-only loss masking” are currently more detailed than the outcome.

items.says: Combine this bullet with the later loss-masking bullet or distinguish the work.
items.because: The two bullets describe closely related work.

items.says: Define “reviewer disagreement” more precisely.
items.because: The reader needs to understand what the reported reduction means.

items.says: Say whether the reduction was measured on held-out cases, production cases, or an internal audit.
items.because: The measurement setting is unclear.

items.says: Clarify any effect of the routing on recall, coverage, or latency.
items.because: The reader needs to know whether limiting agents introduced tradeoffs.

items.says: Make the roles of the specialists and independent reviewer easier to follow.
items.because: The sentence is dense.

items.says: Define “equal accuracy” with an evaluation metric.
items.because: The credibility of the result depends on a clearly controlled comparison.

items.says: Clarify exactly what baseline the latency result was compared against.
items.because: The comparison needs to be clearly controlled.

items.says: Include the number of cases or rollouts used for the comparison if available.
items.because: It would help establish the comparison’s credibility.

items.says: Simplify the reward-design detail if it is not central to the role.
items.because: The combination of training methods, rewards, and results is information-dense.

items.says: Clarify whether the harness was used beyond your team.
items.because: Its scope of adoption is unclear.

items.says: Explain how the regressions were found and whether they were prevented from release.
items.because: The practical consequence of the harness is unclear.

items.says: Add evaluation runtime, automation level, or test-case count if possible.
items.because: It would make the engineering contribution more concrete.

items.says: Remove this bullet or distinguish it from the first Mobility Systems bullet.
items.because: It repeats the loss-masking detail without adding a measurable accomplishment.

items.says: Add a separate experiment, behavior improvement, or evaluation finding if the bullet stays.
items.because: As written, it describes a method rather than an outcome.

items.says: Do not imply that loss masking improved faithfulness without a measured result.
items.because: The claimed improvement is not supported here by a measurement.

items.says: Resolve the apparent duplication of the backlog accomplishment under the Research-Agent project.
items.because: The repeated triage-branch and sensor-signal claim creates a credibility problem.

items.says: Clarify your individual contribution rather than the team’s contribution.
items.because: The impact needs to be tied clearly to your work.

items.says: Explain the baseline and measurement period for the 68% backlog reduction.
items.because: The basis for the impact figure is unclear.

items.says: Move this bullet earlier if it is the largest production impact.
items.because: The strongest measurable outcomes should come first.

items.says: Reduce the Mobility Systems internship to four or five bullets.
items.because: Six bullets is somewhat long for one internship, especially when two overlap.

items.says: Clarify exactly what the “4x” GPU-memory reduction means.
items.because: The size of the reduction is ambiguous.

items.says: Explain what the memory reduction enabled.
items.because: Its practical consequence is missing.

items.says: Clarify hardware support for BF16 and whether model quality changed.
items.because: The quality tradeoff and deployment context are missing.

items.says: Specify the workload, request volume, or endpoint for the latency result.
items.because: Additional scope would make the optimization’s scale easier to judge.

items.says: Say whether the 200 ms build threshold covers all relevant endpoints or just one.
items.because: The scope of the test is unclear.

items.says: Mention cache correctness or freshness safeguards if relevant.
Correct the tense mismatch between “Maintained” and “adds.”
items.because: The grammar issue makes the line look less polished.

items.says: Clarify whether you implemented the regression checks or maintained an existing pipeline.
items.because: The bullet does not make your change to the pipeline clear.

items.says: Explain whether release cycles were reduced to three days or standardized at three days.
items.because: The release-speed result is ambiguous.

items.says: Quantify failures caught by the regression checks if possible.
items.because: The bullet does not clearly connect the automation to its outcome.

items.says: Clarify whether you designed the queue architecture or implemented the migration.
items.because: Your role in the migration is unclear.

items.says: Quantify the reliability or dispatch improvement if available.
items.because: The operational and business impact remains somewhat qualitative.

items.says: Explain how removal of the nightly backlogs was observed or measured.
items.because: The current wording does not establish the measurement.

items.says: Verify that “Owner” reflects your role and that the project is still active.
items.because: Both claims need to be accurate for the listed date.

items.says: Add a link if the project is public and sufficiently documented.
Indicate usage, contributor, user, or test scale if possible.
items.because: That would give a personal or open-source project more context.

items.says: Replace the broad “AI-first engineering practices” claim with a concrete technical or adoption result.
items.because: It is promotional and unsupported by a measurable result.

items.says: Support “accelerating delivery” and “improving outcomes” with concrete measurements or remove them.
items.because: They read as general claims rather than evidence of engineering work.

items.says: Define “working context” and how it was measured.
items.because: The measurement terms are ambiguous.

items.says: Define what grew “100x” and the unit used for that comparison.
items.because: The unusually large growth claim may invite skepticism without a clear definition.

items.says: Describe the evaluation setup for the 100-turn stress test.
items.because: The reader needs to know whether the test is meaningful.

items.says: Include a measured effect on cost, latency, task success, or failures if available.
items.because: That would establish the practical result.

items.says: Quantify the improvement in failures, deadlocks, throughput, or successful runs.
items.because: The claimed benefit is currently qualitative.

items.says: Say whether the fix was tested in production, a load test, or a synthetic stress test.
items.because: Test evidence would make the result more credible.

items.says: Define what “50-way fan-out” counts.
items.because: It is unclear whether it means agents, tool calls, requests, or tasks.

items.says: Name the categories or types of citation and faithfulness metrics.
items.because: They may not be obvious from the project title.

items.says: Clarify whether you implemented metrics, integrated existing ones, or built their interface.
items.because: “Integrated” can describe a wide range of contribution levels.

items.says: Say whether the work was merged upstream or used by external contributors.
items.because: Open-source adoption would make the contribution stronger.

items.says: Use the precise statistical-measure name and add confidence or significance information if available.
items.because: The validation result needs clearer statistical context.

items.says: Explain the degradation protocol and what the evaluator score represented.
items.because: The reader needs to distinguish evaluator validity from correlation caused by the test construction.

items.says: Clarify whether the 400-plus trials were independent reports, repeated runs, or multiple perturbations.
items.because: The experimental design is not fully clear.

items.says: Remove or distinguish the backlog claim duplicated under Mobility Systems.
items.because: Repeating the same accomplishment can make the résumé appear padded or inconsistent.

items.says: If this is separate work, explain how its triage branch differs from the production diagnostics system.
items.because: A project should add new evidence rather than repeat the internship achievement.

items.says: Make the ownership and timeline of this project result explicit.
items.because: They are needed to distinguish it from the internship work.

items.says: Git is listed as a programming language even though it is a tool.
items.because: Languages, tools, and frameworks should be distinguishable.

items.says: Organize the skills into clearer categories.
items.because: The current category mixes languages and a tool.

items.says: Add central model-serving, data-processing, testing, or infrastructure tools if genuinely known.
items.because: Those tools may better represent the experience shown.

items.says: Make “agent evaluation” more specific.
items.because: The term is broad and should convey the evaluation capabilities you mean.

items.says: Use consistent date formatting throughout.
Check verb tense across completed roles and ongoing projects.
items.because: Completed work should use past tense and ongoing work present tense.

items.says: Avoid awkward wrapping of hyphenated terms such as “dead-letter.”
items.because: Visual breaks can hurt presentation.

items.says: Restore real company and university names if these are review anonymizations.
items.because: The actual résumé should use real names unless confidentiality requires otherwise.

items.says: Make advanced technical terms understandable enough for a non-specialist recruiter.
items.because: The résumé uses many such terms, and the outcome should remain identifiable.
